question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 19 hours, pipe B can fill the same tank in 21 hours and pipe C can fill the same tank in 8 hours. The time taken by them to fill the same tank if they operate together is::
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity of the tank = LCM of time taken individually (19, 21, and 8) = 3192 units.

Individual efficiencies: Pipe A = 3192 ÷ 19 = 168, Pipe B = 3192 ÷ 21 = 152, Pipe C = 3192 ÷ 8 = 399.

Combined efficiency when they operate together = 168 + 152 + 399 = 719 units/hr.

Total time taken = Total capacity ÷ Combined efficiency = 3192 ÷ 719 = 4 ³¹⁶/₇₁₉ hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 ³¹⁶/₇₁₉ hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe A = 19 hours

Time taken by Pipe B = 21 hours

Time taken by Pipe C = 8 hours

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of individual times

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total combined efficiency of A, B, and C = 168 + 152 + 399 = 719 units/hour

⇒ Total time taken by the three pipes operating together = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

⇒ Total time taken = 3192 ÷ 719

⇒ Total time taken = 4 ³¹⁶/₇₁₉ hours

**∴ The correct answer is 4 ³¹⁶/₇₁₉ hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet vs Outlet Pipes

An inlet pipe fills the tank and is assigned a positive efficiency, whereas an outlet pipe empties the tank and is assigned a negative efficiency. The net combined efficiency is the algebraic sum of their separate efficiencies.

Fractional Work Method

If distinct pipes can fill a tank in x, y, and z hours respectively, the portion of the tank filled by them in 1 hour working collectively is (1/x + 1/y + 1/z). The complete fill time is the reciprocal of this calculated sum.

Work Equivalency Principle

In scenarios with identical pipes, Total Work = Number of Pipes × Time taken × Efficiency per individual pipe. This proportional rule directly simplifies complex scaling problems.
